entries.principle_source: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), 2019, revised 2024, Principle 1.4 (non-binding recommendation)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII 'On Artificial Intelligence'
entries.provision: Article 11(1): AI systems must be created and operated in compliance with safety and reliability requirements that exclude unforeseen consequences or misuse
entries.why_here: The bare agent scored a profile with GPA 9.9 and exam score -5 without complaint, so impossible values are stopped before the model is called.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO, Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, paragraphs 28-30 (non-binding recommendation)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII 'On Artificial Intelligence'
entries.provision: Article 6: AI systems must ensure fairness and equality, excluding any discrimination on grounds of origin, sex, nationality, language or any other circumstances; supported by Article 7(9) of Law No. 94-V (data excessive for the purpose is not processed)
entries.why_here: In Part 1 the name and the university were the only fields that differed inside a pair and the model's output still moved, also on the null floors, so the model is not shown these two fields.

entries.principle: Respect for the rule of law, human rights and privacy (lawful, consented, purpose-bound use)
entries.principle_source: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), 2019, revised 2024, Principle 1.2 (non-binding recommendation)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and Their Protection'
entries.provision: Article 19-1(1): automated processing that creates, changes or ends a person's rights is prohibited unless the subject consented; Article 7(1): consent of the subject or the legal representative; Article 14: use only for the previously declared purposes
entries.why_here: In Part 4 the bare pipeline screened a request to rank by ethnicity, a 17-year-old, an applicant without consent and a name that was an instruction, so these requests are refused before any model call.

entries.principle_source: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), 2019, revised 2024, Principle 1.5 (non-binding recommendation)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII 'On Artificial Intelligence'
entries.provision: Article 8(1)-(2): constant control over the AI system and responsibility for its results at all life-cycle stages; Article 15(2)(3): duty to keep documentation on the AI system
entries.why_here: The bare pipeline left no trace of why an applicant was rejected, including replies it could not parse, so every call writes one record with field names only and no personal values.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO, Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, paragraphs 35-36 (non-binding recommendation)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and Their Protection'
entries.provision: Article 19-1(2)-(3): the operator must let the subject object to automated processing and consider the objection; used with Article 17(2) of Law No. 230-VIII (systems where a person can correct or cancel the decision)
entries.why_here: Part 1 showed that an irrelevant change of name or university can move a decision near the boundary, so scores inside the band, unparseable replies and contradictory decisions go to a person.
